name: Vibration sensor
summary: Sensor on a machine bearing that measures vibration and feeds a monitor or relay for alarm and trip.
description: A vibration sensor is mounted on a machine bearing housing or near the shaft and produces a signal related to vibration, either as raw acceleration or as a processed velocity output in a 4-20 mA loop. It feeds condition monitoring systems and machine protection relays that alarm and trip large motors, generators and fans.

Accelerometers, velocity sensors and non-contact proximity probes measure different things and suit different machines. The symbol does not show which type is used, the measuring axis or the alarm levels, which are machine-specific and should be in the instrument schedule.
readingNotes: Identify sensor type and measuring axis.
Find the alarm and trip levels in the monitoring settings.
distinction: A vibration sensor produces a measurement signal; a vibration switch only changes a contact at a set level.
